item.title: Record Store Day 2026 Report: ‘Biggest Year Ever’ for Many Retailers as Taylor Swift, Charli xcx & More Titles Fly Off Shelves
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music trends. Today, we're talking about Record Store Day, or RSD, and the impact it had on indie record stores across the US.
On April 18th, record stores saw a surge in sales, with some even declaring it their best day ever. Rough Trade Records in Manhattan, Down In The Valley in Minneapolis, and Music Millennium in Portland, Oregon, were just a few of the stores that reported record-breaking sales.
The big hits of the day were RSD titles from popular artists like Taylor Swift, Bruce Springsteen, and Pink Floyd. According to Luminate, physical album sales reached 2.276 million units in the US, slightly higher than last year's 2.241 million units.
[Short music break]
Host: But what made this year's RSD so special? We spoke to Stephen Godfrey, co-owner and president of Rough Trade, who said it was their biggest year ever, even beating out their flagship store in London. Rough Trade's Indieplaza event at Rockefeller Center featured eight bands and three DJs, making for a fun-filled day that drew in huge crowds.
[Short music break]
Host: The numbers are in, and while vinyl sales were slightly lower than last year, CD sales were higher, with 627,000 units sold compared to 519,000 last year. Overall, it was a fantastic day for record stores, and we can't wait to see what next year's RSD brings.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. If you're a music lover, be sure to check out your local record store and support the music community. Until next time, keep on spinning!
